💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, we all know AI can get expensive.
  • Also: Microsoft indicates its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
  • It has been revealed that earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, we all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

Also: Microsoft indicates its latest AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

It has been revealed that earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

According to recent reports, if it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s major bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions.

To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:.

The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

Instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

Industry observers note that then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s new.

What comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically indicates, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”.

In other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving company labor costs with every token processed.

In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the organization saved any real money.

Also: 5 reasons your company needs a chief AI officer in 2026.

According to recent reports, I find it particularly telling that this is from the organization that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

It has been revealed that that’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

Sources indicate that microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

With Agent 365 and the tech giant’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:.

It has been revealed that this means the company doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the manufacturer’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella revealed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft claims its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

“As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft remarked. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also unveiled Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft stated, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s newly introduced Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft noted the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft noted.

The tech giant added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Nadella also unveiled a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Right now in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up quickly,” Microsoft remarked of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

According to recent reports, microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can quickly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft announced a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

In a recent development, agent 365, which Microsoft unveiled last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft revealed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

According to recent reports, “It starts with a fresh way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft said. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

In a recent development, “Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft mentioned. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise aims.

Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I loved journaling as a child.
  • It has been revealed that I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success.
  • Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I loved journaling as a child. It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst. Then college called, and I moved to a different country, leaving behind my childhood, my Nirvana cassettes (I’m old, OK?) and, sadly, my journaling habit.

It has been revealed that I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success. I’ve delved into bullet journals under the pretense of improving my productivity, but I gave up when it became too much effort. I’ve invested in multiple notebooks and planners, only to eventually neglect them.

Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.

It all began when I discovered the wondrous world of journaling TikTok. In short-form videos, creators would show off beautiful journal pages decorated with colored markers, stickers, washi tape and, yes, photos — specifically photos from portable printers because the prints are small enough to fit within the confines of a typical journal or planner. I really liked the idea of decking out my journal pages with photos of my everyday life. I knew I had to get one.

Recent findings suggest that after a bit of research, I decided on a couple of criteria. First, I wanted the printer to be a dye sublimation printer rather than a ZINK (Zero Ink) printer. Dye sublimation printers essentially use heat to transfer dye onto the paper, while ZINK printers use a special paper that activates under heat with no ink required (hence the name). Dye sublimation prints tend to be higher quality because it transfers the dye in layers of cyan, magenta and yellow, followed by a protective coating.

Second, I wanted the photo to be on sticky paper so that I didn’t have to mess around with glue to add these photos to my journal.

I found quite a number of dye sublimation pocket printers on the market, but the one that caught my eye immediately was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2 pocket printer. I fell in love with it the moment I saw it. The sleek white design, the Polaroid logo and that curved rainbow accent on the edge really sealed the deal for me. Call me a sucker for style, I guess.

Industry observers note that I purchased a Hi-Print 2×3 “starter set,” which includes the printer along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge has 10 photo sheets, and each sheet is made out of sticky back photo paper, which is exactly what I wanted. Both the Gen 2 and the prior Gen 1 are easy to find; the main difference is the newer one uses a USB-C charging port while the original uses the older Micro-USB port.

Industry observers note that getting started with the printer is simple enough: Download the Polaroid Hi-Print app, pair the printer with your phone and you’re ready to go. The app is fairly easy to navigate. I like that it lets you arrange your photos in collages so you’re not limited to just one photo per sheet. You can also decorate your prints with colorful frames or decorations. The printer even offers a mosaic option that lets you print out one substantial image using multiple sheets.

Industry observers note that since it’s a dye sublimation printer, the Hi-Print prints out photos in stages. It lays down the different colors in multiple passes (yellow in the first pass, magenta in the second pass, and so forth). Because of that, printing does take a while: around 60 seconds per photo.

Sources indicate that but I don’t mind the delay, as the resulting photo quality is superb. The colors are vibrant and the overall image is nice and sharp. The contrast could be a little better, but for a little pocket printer, the quality definitely exceeded my expectations.

Sources indicate that there are a few downsides, however. The obvious one is that photo cartridges can be pretty expensive. One pack of 20 sheets is around $17, though you can get it for $14 each if you buy the 5-pack. That’s still almost 70 cents per 2×3 print. If you use multiple prints, that can add up pretty quickly.

Sources indicate that another downside is that it doesn’t have a super long battery life. It only has a 620mAh battery, which Polaroid says will last up to 20 photo printing sessions. I only ever use this printer at home, so this isn’t a big deal for me, but I can see this being a potential disappointment if you want to bring this printer on the road. That mentioned, if you do want to charge it, it doesn’t take that long. Polaroid says it takes under an hour, and that feels about right based on my experience.

I’ve had this printer for a few months now, and I’m very pleased with it. Since I use the photos primarily with my journal, I also really appreciate how thin the photo sheets are, so they don’t bulk up the pages too much. I truly enjoy printing out my little creations, cutting out my collages and then decorating my journal with them.

I might not have my childhood back nor my Nirvana cassettes, but at least I’ve finally recaptured the joys of journaling — even if it did require a bit of help from a pocket printer.

#73934. Breaking: MSCI Is Cutting Strategy and Metaplanet From Its Indexes. Here's What It Means for Bitcoin Treasury Tech giant Stocks.

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (873 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: MSCI Is Cutting Strategy and Metaplanet From Its Indexes. Here's What It Means for Bitcoin Treasury Tech giant Stocks.

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (873 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • MSCI (MSCI -2.22%) made it official on Nov.
  • Sources indicate that the decision caps a fight that has run for more than a year.
  • Recent findings suggest that I went back to Strategy's formal response, and wow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Anders Bylund – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:17PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Strategy ›.

MSCI (MSCI -2.22%) made it official on Nov. 11. Strategy (MSTR -9.67%), the software company turned Bitcoin (BTC +2.00%) treasury, will be deleted from the MSCI USA Index at the close of Nov. 30. Japan-based Bitcoin treasury peer Metaplanet (MTPLF -10.78%) is also on its way out, and Ethereum (ETH +3.75%) treasury company SharpLink (SBET -9.13%) lands on a latest public watch list.

Sources indicate that the decision caps a fight that has run for more than a year. In October 2025, the market index manager proposed excluding any manufacturer whose digital-asset holdings made up 50% or more of total assets. More than 250 organizations objected, and MSCI dropped the idea in January. In August, it came back with a broader screen aimed at "non-operating companies," built on five financial-ratio flags. Trip four of them, and you're out.

Recent findings suggest that I went back to Strategy's formal response, and wow. The letter calls the proposal "pretextual," suggesting that MSCI may be inventing reasons to exclude Strategy. The letter points out that this firm alone makes up about 87% of the market value affected across all six names on the list of exclusions. Strategy insists that its Bitcoin business is an operating segment of an established software company, a treatment it indicates followed discussions with SEC staff.

Fair points, some of them. When a supposedly neutral rule lands that heavily on one name, it's tough to call it a coincidence. It's like announcing a upcoming dress code that happens to ban exactly one guest's unusual hat.

It has been revealed that then again, the same 10-page letter indicates the exclusion would have "no meaningful impact" on Strategy's business. If it really doesn't matter, that's a lot of footnotes for a shrug.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Strategy held a special investor call on Nov. 19, eight days after the announcement. Executive Chairman Michael Saylor and CEO Phong Le spent the hour on preferred stock, credit markets, and Bitcoin-per-share metrics. The index removal never came up.

It has been revealed that instead, the focus was the Strategy Stretch (STRC -1.01%) preferred stock. Le remarked Strategy has bought back about $3 billion of Stretch at $95 to $99 per share, after selling it on the open market at $100 per share. Saylor estimated that organic demand for the 12% instrument has shrunk from about $10.5 billion six months ago to roughly $7 billion today. The buybacks are meant to find that floor.

But no analysts asked questions on that call, and management never uttered the word "MSCI" on this seemingly convenient stage. The silence spoke volumes.

It has been revealed that strategy's homepage is now essentially a Bitcoin cockpit, full of data on MSTR stock and the organization's Bitcoin holdings. That's a strange look for a company that still sells analytics software, but the numbers are useful:.

That last one is the real gut punch. The market values Strategy at about 63% of its Bitcoin holdings. Even after subtracting $19.4 billion of debt and preferred stock, the stock trades at a slight discount to what's left.

The premium shimmer that let Strategy print stock and buy coins hand over fist has faded. Saylor himself notes the stock-for-Bitcoin trade needs roughly a 1.29x multiple to make sense. There's a canyon between the existing mNAV and the required one.

Index funds tracking MSCI benchmarks will have to sell their Strategy and Metaplanet shares by the end of November. Some of that selling was likely priced in after the August proposal, but forced selling is never handled with velvet gloves.

The bigger matter is precedent. Other index providers, such as the S&P Dow Jones Indices group, have not adopted MSCI's screen. Strategy could still qualify for the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) index someday (if it meets many other requirements). But now there's a template that the others could follow. Any organization that builds its balance sheet around a single digital asset has to consider that the passive-investing bid may not be a given.

Metaplanet goes out the door with Strategy on Nov. 30, and SharpLink is standing in the hallway. The copycats that built their businesses on Saylor's playbook are learning that the operating strategy didn't come with an index guarantee.

Sources indicate that strategy isn't in trouble tomorrow. It has $4.7 billion in U.S. dollar reserves, which covers about 3.4 years of interest and dividends. That's a meaningful cash cushion.

But a cushion isn't a catalyst. Without the index bid, and trading at a discount to its own Bitcoin reserves, the old flywheel has stalled. The interesting question isn't whether Strategy survives. It's what it takes to bring back the lost mNAV premium.

It has been revealed that when our analyst team has a stock tip, it can pay to listen. After all, Stock Advisor's total average return is 719%* — a market-crushing outperformance compared to 192% for the S&P 500.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant.
  • Also: Microsoft notes its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • Sources indicate that MAI noted it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella revealed several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft notes its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

Sources indicate that MAI noted it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, remarked during the keynote.

According to recent reports, the approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft noted it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman remarked during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

In a recent development, the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the company has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Industry observers note that western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the newly introduced coding model the organization unveiled at Ignite.

In a recent development, the manufacturer also released its latest image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

#73929. Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2221 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2221 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
  • According to recent reports, microsoft Outlook?
  • Recent findings suggest that something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

According to recent reports, microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some issues. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

Recent findings suggest that something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these complications, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

It has been revealed that adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at cybersecurity manufacturer CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

“This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

One major reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

Sources indicate that if it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

Industry observers note that artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a significant or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

At the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

Even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should patch. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

Another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

When I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he noted, “it’s bad.”.

Recent findings suggest that as owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He indicates he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. Newly introduced AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

“You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand said.

According to recent reports, things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning last week.

In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers says CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

“Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers noted.

Sources indicate that despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

“The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” remarked Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

Recent findings suggest that AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

According to recent reports, the good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

It still might not be enough, and Significant Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman remarked he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

Sources indicate that and defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella noted this week at the Upcoming York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

That’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

“There’s effectively this substantial backlog of security issues in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” remarked Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity firm focused on connected devices.

It has been revealed that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

“Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse mentioned.

Sources indicate that wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of complications is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with vital, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to revision so frequently these days.

“It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” said Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

In a recent development, and patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s challenges on Tuesday.

Things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents new problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing concern.

In the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

It has been revealed that major Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

“I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” noted Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy claims.

In a recent development, that means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into new software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

Recent findings suggest that the main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

“I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he mentioned. “It will hurt a bit.”.

Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more important than ever.

“You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers stated. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

But consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a organization isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

We don’t have to put up with it, Barlet says. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he stated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:25PM EST.
  • According to recent reports, investors often weigh growth potential against current profitability when comparing Airbnb (ABNB -1.41%) and DoorDash (DASH -2.88%).
  • Airbnb focuses on the global travel market by connecting hosts with guests seeking unique accommodations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:25PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Airbnb ›.

According to recent reports, investors often weigh growth potential against current profitability when comparing Airbnb (ABNB -1.41%) and DoorDash (DASH -2.88%). Both companies have transformed how consumers spend on experiences and daily conveniences, but their financial trajectories remain distinct.

Airbnb focuses on the global travel market by connecting hosts with guests seeking unique accommodations. DoorDash operates a local commerce platform that facilitates delivery from restaurants and retail merchants. While both benefit from digital shifts, their cost structures and capital requirements differ significantly.

Industry observers note that airbnb operates a two-sided global marketplace that connects more than 5 million hosts with guests across roughly 220 countries. The organization focuses on expanding its brand through strategic partnerships with cultural and entertainment organizations to attract a diverse range of travelers. This positioning within consumer discretionary stocks allows it to capture spending on both short-term vacations and long-term stays.

Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $13.9 billion, representing growth of approximately 16.7% over the prior year. The organization demonstrated significant bottom-line strength by generating a net income of close to $3.2 billion during this same period. This level of profitability is a hallmark of its asset-light business model, which avoids the costs of owning physical properties.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

According to recent reports, doorDash operates a local commerce platform that connects merchants, consumers, and delivery couriers across more than 40 countries. The company has evolved beyond restaurant delivery into grocery and convenience sectors, maintaining agreements with over 600,000 merchants. Growth is further supported by over 56 million monthly active users and a proposed $17 billion acquisition of Instacart to solidify its market position.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $17.1 billion, which is a significant 35% increase compared to the previous twelve-month period. The company also reached a milestone by reporting a net income of approximately $1.1 billion.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Airbnb faces intense competition from established online travel agencies like Booking Holdings (BKNG -1.64%) and Expedia Group (EXPE -1.77%), as well as traditional hotel chains. The manufacturer is also subject to evolving legal and regulatory environments, particularly restrictive short-term rental laws in major markets like Upcoming York City. Additionally, reliance on third-party payment processors and other threats present ongoing operational risks.

It has been revealed that doorDash contends with fierce competition from other delivery platforms and merchants who develop their own direct-to-consumer ordering systems. The business model faces regulatory scrutiny regarding the classification of couriers as independent contractors, which could significantly impact labor costs. Furthermore, the manufacturer relies on third-party service providers like Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) Web Services for its platform stability and faces integration risks from its large-scale acquisition of Instacart.

Airbnb appears more attractive based on future earnings estimates, while DoorDash carries a lower valuation when compared to its sales.

DoorDash has a strong presence in the delivery space, but between DoorDash and Airbnb, I'd lean more toward Airbnb as an investable opportunity.

It has been revealed that one reason is that Airbnb is simply more profitable. While DoorDash's net income in the third quarter of 2026 climbed 91% to $466 million, it still pales in comparison to Airbnb's net income in the same quarter, at $1.9 billion. The other reason is that Airbnb's opportunities for expansion and revenue growth look more appealing. While DoorDash is acquiring Instacart, its platform is still more about restaurants, groceries, and broad delivery services. In comparison, Airbnb has more opportunities for expansion and integration that can lead to meaningful revenue growth by bundling car rentals, travel planning, and experiences into its offerings.

Sources indicate that to get an idea of what to expect from Airbnb stock over the near term, analysts generally have a favorable outlook. According to CNN-tracked data, of the 46 analysts who cover the stock, 57% rate it a buy, 41% a hold, and 2% a sell. Of those analysts, the median one-year stock price forecast is $211, representing a gain of 23.8% from the price as of this writing, $170.36. The group's highest target is $245, representing a 43.8% gain, while the lowest target, $161, would be a 5.4% loss. While stock price forecasts aren't guarantees, the lowest projection indicates a 5% loss, so the risk-to-reward framework looks favorable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

Industry observers note that but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is right now expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

Recent findings suggest that this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

It has been revealed that one thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:.

With the repository added, you can install it with:.

Once installed, you can use it as expected.

As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

Sources indicate that it’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

Also: Linux has hundreds of distros: 5 reasons to stop using the same few.

It’s been a very long time since Canonical had a disappointing release, and 27.04 will keep up that trend.

#73925. One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1104 w)
📖 Baca

One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1104 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago.
  • In a recent development, how many times can we fold the iPhone Duo?
  • Sources indicate that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago. Every day since then, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, a dedicated machine inside CNET’s lab has been folding and unfolding it over and over again. For science.

In a recent development, how many times can we fold the iPhone Duo? As of Friday, Nov. 20, we’re up to more than 565,000 folds and the Duo hasn’t broken yet. The hinge has shown signs of potential failure, however. Our technicians, as well as the cameras and sensors that are part of our testing rig, continue to monitor the situation and collect data.

Sources indicate that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky. My team and I designed and built this proprietary machine to test foldable phones like Apple’s and its Samsung rival, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which we’ve also started testing). I’ve worked on the methodology and build of this testing rig for months in anticipation of Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone.

We even named our machine to match its purpose: Meet the Fold-a-Phone.

My team of engineers and testing experts has been watching the iPhone Duo open and close, over and over, for the past few weeks to rigorously and systematically monitor the durability of Apple’s hinge and two screens.

After all, repeatedly folding a phone with bare hands can only get you so far in understanding the complex forces at play between the magnetics that snap the screen shut and the all-critical hinge.

According to recent reports, CNET’s Senior Technology Reporter, Abrar Al-Heeti, has done a beautiful job capturing the iPhone Duo’s pros and cons in her smart, thorough review as well as her one-month-later follow-up. Our Fold-a-Phone machine will add a deep data foundation to complement her real-world experience.

Since Apple hasn’t publicly shared claims of the iPhone Duo’s foldable lifespan, CNET’s Fold-a-Phone machine is poised to provide a wealth of valuable data about Apple’s first foldable phone and competing models in the foldable market.

And yes, you’d better believe we will use our treasure trove of in-house data to share status updates and comparisons during our ongoing testing window with the Duo.

According to recent reports, join CNET’s iPhone Duo livestream on YouTube weekdays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. ET, where you can follow along live and watch the Fold-a-Phone do its thing to a Duo.

The importance of this moment is hard to overstate. Apple’s appearance on the foldable smartfold frontier lags Samsung by seven years (the first Galaxy Fold went on sale in the US in September 2019). Motorola and other phone-makers have long experimented with foldable phones in every shape and size, including a trifold accordion foldable phone we first demoed in 2019.

CNET’s mobile experts, including Al-Heeti and Editor at Large Andrew Lanxon, have discussed the legitimizing effect of the iPhone Duo’s existence on the entire foldable phone landscape, which has previously felt like a newly introduced-wave fantasy rather than a mainstream riptide.

Sources indicate that in many ways, Apple’s newfound competition with existing foldable phones completes the portfolio. That is precisely why we’re building the Fold-a-Phone now, and why our proprietary machine, methodology and test data will enrich our collective understanding of the capabilities – and yes, limitations – of foldable phones as our true next-generation mobile device.

Most current foldable phones are rated for 200,000 to 500,000 folds. As such, we knew we needed to create a robust and adaptable machine that could accommodate book- and flip-style foldable phones of any size, dimension and hinge orientation. (Note: The Fold-a-Phone was not built for trifold phones, which present a unique element to the engineering challenge.).

Moreover, we wanted to test the phone the way people would actually use it. No one just sits around opening and closing their foldable phone at top speed all day. Rather, you open it naturally, spend a few minutes watching a video, browsing a web page, or using an app, close it, and then put it in your pocket. This may happen dozens of times per day.

Mimicking this usage on the Fold-a-Phone limits undue stress on the phone hinge and avoids generating excess heat compared to a test built for speed.

We determined that a cadence of roughly 4 seconds could sidestep technical hurdles while also being reasonably fast. The foldable phone takes 1 second to open, 1 second to fully open, 1 second to close and 1 second to fully close. This cycle counts as a single completed fold. Then, the cycle repeats until either the hinge or the screen gives out.

In conceptualizing and building the Fold-a-Phone, our team has used standard, off-the-shelf components to simplify the machine’s development. The essential design consists of two armatures, distinctly designed to perform the opening and closing movements with both force and grace.

According to recent reports, an industrial-grade stepper motor drives each armature, with the host software (running on a connected computer) deterministically adjusting the torque to complete each step of the process while also protecting the phone. If any of the several proximity sensors fail to detect the armature in the correct position, the machine stops immediately.

In a recent development, we also monitor the motors’ power usage to track how well the foldable phone opens and closes over time. We have set up cameras to capture images and video of the test from multiple angles, and we will analyze regular status updates from the computer to determine the current status of the phone and the test.

To ensure we never miss a major development, the entire rig is connected to an EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus power station to guard against electricity outages, and all the output data is saved to multiple locations.

To secure each phone to the machine, we use our CNET Lab Test-winning 3D printer, the Prusa Core One, to 3D-print a custom “sled” that matches each phone’s exact dimensions. We secure the phone to the sled with heavy-duty double-sided tape (yes, it works!) and then screw the sled onto the machine.

There’s always room for improvement. We’re constantly looking for ways to make the machine run more smoothly and quietly without disrupting the folding rhythm.

Industry observers note that apple’s presence is already changing the game and could very well spur innovation in ways we can’t predict today. But until then, our Fold-a-Phone machine will continue to test the iPhone Duo and its competitors, and CNET’s writers will report on how well these individual hinged devices stand up to the challenge – or fold under pressure.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 21, 2026 at 2:27PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Tractor Supply ›.

Shortly after buying Berkshire Hathaway (BRKB -0.36%)(BRKA -0.47%), Warren Buffett picked up a Baltimore department store because it looked like a bargain. Three years later, he wrote that he "was lucky to sell the business for about what I had paid." His lesson became one of his most quoted lines: "It's far better to buy a wonderful tech giant at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.".

I keep coming back to that rule, because one of my favorite unglamorous retailers finally has a fair price.

It has been revealed that tractor Supply (TSCO -0.77%) sells what rural life runs on: animal feed, pet food, fencing, and tools. It's the largest rural lifestyle retailer in the U.S., with nearly 2,500 stores.

It has been revealed that this year has been bumpy. A rough May dragged down the second quarter, and the company cut its outlook in July. Bigger purchases remain soft, and CEO Hal Lawton mentioned, "Elevated interest rates and reduced housing mobility are weighing on property improvements and larger projects.".

Sources indicate that the everyday stuff held up, though. Consumables like animal feed and bedding beat the store average, and same-store sales went from negative in July to growing by September. Neighbor's Club loyalty members made up nearly 82% of sales, and CFO Kurt Barton put it plainly: "Tractor Supply remains a differentiated business with significant competitive advantages." A crowd that loyal is my kind of economic moat.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Management isn't waiting around. It used tariff refunds to cut prices on about 50 everyday essentials, raised its Freshpet cooler rollout to about 1,000 stores, and now has its Allivet pharmacy filling prescriptions for VIP Petcare, the mobile vet business it bought. On Nov. 12, it joined the platform of Uber Technologies, so shoppers can get dog food or garden supplies delivered. "The need for convenience doesn't stop at the city limits," mentioned Uber retail executive Nathan Bernheim, while Tractor Supply digital chief Matthew Rubin noted that "millions of Uber users have a new way to discover Tractor Supply.".

Not every bet paid off. The manufacturer closed 74 money-losing Petsense pet stores last quarter, and higher fuel and freight costs squeezed margins.

The stock sits about 30% below its 52-week high at roughly 21 times earnings. That's no bargain-bin P/E ratio, and Buffett's rule claims it doesn't need to be. A $1,000 investment buys about 25 shares, and capital spending should drop below 4% of sales next year, freeing up cash for shareholders.

"Whether it is preparing for winter, caring for their animals, or maintaining their homes and properties, we have an important and critical role to play in their lives," Lawton stated.

In that 1989 letter, Buffett also wrote that "time is the friend of the wonderful business." For a store people need every week, I'm happy to give it that time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining new traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

Industry observers note that gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

Sources indicate that bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

Sources indicate that the U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

In a recent development, the Treasury Department remarked last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the prepares.

Last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "big toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

According to recent reports, long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

According to recent reports, "Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold stated in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Sources indicate that the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah noted. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah said. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Sources indicate that coltman at 21Shares mentioned the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

Deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

Billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder noted.

"The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

It has been revealed that on Friday, Google’s Gemini team unveiled the results of a upcoming partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

Recent findings suggest that the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more quickly and enable first responders to upgrade maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

“This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” said Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.”.

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google notes the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations.

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” remarked Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

Sources indicate that one metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

The Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

The integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

According to recent reports, salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a fresh brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

Retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

Shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

Recent findings suggest that 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

The survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

According to recent reports, the majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

In a recent development, retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

Sources indicate that today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may right now be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

Sources indicate that if you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

You’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

If you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

It has been revealed that the PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing fresh game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.
