  • Sources indicate that choosing between high-growth consumer favorites can be difficult for long-term investors.
  • CAVA is disrupting the fast-casual dining space with its Mediterranean-focused menu and expanding grocery line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seena Hassouna – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 2:34PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Cava Group ›.

Sources indicate that choosing between high-growth consumer favorites can be difficult for long-term investors. Both CAVA Group (CAVA -4.67%) and On (ONON -2.76%) are scaling swiftly, but which stock is the better addition to your portfolio?

CAVA is disrupting the fast-casual dining space with its Mediterranean-focused menu and expanding grocery line. Meanwhile, On is challenging established footwear giants by blending performance technology with high-fashion appeal. While both companies target premium consumers, their financial profiles and valuation multiples vary significantly as they approach the next several years of growth.

According to recent reports, CAVA operates a Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant brand that prioritizes fresh ingredients and customizable bowls. The organization serves a diverse audience, with significant engagement from Millennial and Gen Z consumers across its 500 restaurant locations. Beyond physical dining rooms, the business expands its brand reach by selling dips and spreads through grocery distribution channels.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 4, 2026, revenue reached about $1.4 billion, which represents a 27% increase over the previous year. This rapid top-line growth helped the organization generate a net income of approximately $64.7 million. The upward trend in sales highlights the successful scaling of its restaurant network across 30 states and Washington, D.C.

Industry observers note that the balance sheet indicates a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly 0.6x, which is entirely attributable to restaurant lease obligations, as CAVA has no borrowings. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio is roughly 2.7x, indicating the tech giant has $2.70 in current assets for every dollar of current liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 28, 2025, free cash flow was nearly $26.1 million, representing the cash remaining after a company funds its operations and capital investments. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 8.2% of operating cash flow in the fiscal year ended Dec. 28, 2025.

On designs and sells premium performance footwear and apparel to a global customer base. The firm leverages a multi-channel strategy that includes its own e-commerce platform, 67 physical retail locations, and a vast network of wholesale partners. By focusing on engineering and distinctive design, the brand has established a strong foothold in the Americas, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region.

Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $4.0 billion, an increase of about 17% compared to the prior period. Net income for those 12 months was approximately $526.8 million, resulting in a healthy net margin of roughly 13.1%. This double-digit net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining as profit, suggests strong pricing power in the sportswear market.

Sources indicate that the organization maintains a conservative capital structure with a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.4x as of December 2025, driven by lease obligations rather than borrowings. Its current ratio of nearly 2.7x suggests a strong ability to cover short-term obligations with liquid assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, On generated about CHF 281 million in free cash flow, providing ample capital for further international expansion.

According to recent reports, CAVA faces intense competition from established restaurant chains and other fast-casual brands. The tech giant relies on a limited number of suppliers and single-source partners, which could lead to disruptions if those partners face operational complications. Scaling 500 existing restaurants to a national footprint target of around 1000 also requires significant capital and carries risks related to food safety incidents or cybersecurity compliance.

ON Holdings must contend with fierce rivalry from major global competitors such as Nike and Adidas. Because the brand relies on discretionary spending, any downturn in consumer confidence could negatively affect premium footwear sales. Expanding rapidly into markets like China and Hong Kong also introduces geopolitical and regulatory risks that could affect its global supply chain.

Recent findings suggest that on appears to be the more conservatively priced option because it carries a significantly lower Forward P/E and P/S ratio than CAVA Group. The P/S ratio measures the organization's market value against its sales over the past twelve months.

*Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

On earns the edge because it charges less for the better business. It trades at a lower price-to-sales multiple than CAVA while maintaining several times the net margin, and that gap persists even after you strip out the one-time U.S. tariff refunds that padded its latest quarter. CAVA grew sales last quarter almost entirely by adding restaurants, while guest traffic at existing locations barely moved, and its stock price already assumes that expansion will continue to work. Management blamed part of the slowdown on a produce-safety scare that may fade, but the valuation leaves little cushion if it lingers.On carries its own risks. Wholesale partners in the Americas are ordering more cautiously in a heavily promotional market; fresh Section 301 tariffs are expected to raise costs for its products; and it sells a single discretionary category. Both stocks also trade partly on being trendy, which cuts both ways when consumer tastes turn. I would buy On for 2027, but I would not back up the truck. Build a starter position, add only if the fourth-quarter report shows how much the refunds were hiding and wholesale holds up, and keep CAVA on a watch list until same-restaurant traffic recovers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the biggest horror movies of the year, "Obsession," finally landed on Netflix this week, where Inde Navarrette's unhinged performance will no doubt haunt even more people's nightmares. If you’re still reeling from its tense atmosphere and wonder what other horror movies on Netflix capture that same sense of creeping dread and paranoia, I've got you covered.

Sources indicate that I watch a lot of horror movies, and my top three picks for what to watch after "Obsession" are sure to fit the vibe you're looking for. Two of them come from acclaimed horror series director Mike Flanagan, while the third is a slept-on horror mystery thriller with a perfect 100% score on Rotten Tomatoes that flips the haunted house trope on its head.

So without further ado, let's dive into the best horror movies on Netflix to watch after "Obsession.".

Just like "Obsession," "Hush" is another example of a simple premise executed well. It's also helmed by Mike Flanagan before he established himself as the king of TV horror with "The Haunting of Hill House," "Midnight Mass" and "Carrie." This slasher movie stars Flanagan's wife and long-time collaborator Kate Siegel as Maddie, a deaf and mute woman who becomes the target of a masked killer.

Industry observers note that it's lean, tightly wound horror movie that wrings a surprising amount of tension from its simple premise. The isolated setting of a house in the remote woods also adds to the atmosphere of constant unease, like you're being watched. And while Maddie is relentlessly stalked and tormented by the killer, she's never reduced to a helpless victim, which makes this one of the more empowering genre entries.

It has been revealed that with remarkable direction from Remi Weekes (who also wrote the screenplay), strong performances from the whole cast ("Doctor Who’s" Matt Smith has a small role) and plenty of terrifying moments, "His House" is a certified chiller — and one of the best Netflix horror movies. Whenever I recommend essential horror movies to get non-horror fans into the genre, "His House" tops the list.

Sources indicate that "His House" follows a young refugee couple, Bol (Sope Dirisu) and Rial (Wunmi Mosaku), who are granted asylum in a small English town after fleeing war-torn South Sudan. They struggle to adjust, and straining their relationship further is the supernatural terror haunting their home that seems connected to their past. But while Rial insists something is not right and wants to move, Bol worries that making waves could get them deported. And so the two are left on their own to face whatever's haunting them.

Watch "His House" on Netflix now.

Sources indicate that another one from Flanagan (can you tell I'm a fan?), this trippy horror movie adds a fresh perspective to a familiar framework, where a cursed mirror not only warps the minds of the main characters, but leaves the audience questioning what's real and what's a hallucination. Said mirror is responsible for the deaths of Kaylie (Karen Gillan) and Tim's (Brenton Thwaites) parents, who began acting strange and talking to the apparition of a dark-haired woman (Siegel) before they passed.

According to recent reports, adding to this disorientation, "Oculus" shift between two timelines: when the siblings were young and first witnessing the mirror's horrible influence, and then 11 years later when they come back to put an end to its demented reign of terror for good. Gillan gives a gloriously unhinged performance as her obsession (haha, get it?) with finally proving the mirror's curse is real ends up being her downfall when her carefully laid plans start falling apart.

Industry observers note that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

It has been revealed that also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid prepares, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Major Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

In a recent development, if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The manufacturer already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

According to recent reports, abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent owners may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

Sources indicate that AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Industry observers note that also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

Recent findings suggest that as with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

The feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US customers can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

In a recent development, the change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The new landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

Industry observers note that “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that apple introduced the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the new Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

Apple historically releases an iOS update in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the patch might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

The redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a new Longevity tab and your Health Age.

Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

Live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by upcoming audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

Sources indicate that while both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I said, I still find both features creepy.

And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just stated.

Siri AI gets a huge upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

According to recent reports, you can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

In the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

Each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

Recent findings suggest that standBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

Sources indicate that apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

Sources indicate that if you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a new setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

Here’s where to find the option.

It has been revealed that 1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

If you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have new options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

Industry observers note that next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

It has been revealed that those are a few of the fresh features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not said when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

Here's the Average Social Security Benefit for Men by Age

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:00PM EST.
  • Industry observers note that men's average Social Security benefits run higher than women's at every age.
  • As of December 2025, the most recent data available, the average monthly benefit for men is $2,282.28, according to the Social Security Administration (SSA).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:00PM EST.

Industry observers note that men's average Social Security benefits run higher than women's at every age. This article lays out the numbers to show how those benefits compare across the typical claiming window.

As of December 2025, the most recent data available, the average monthly benefit for men is $2,282.28, according to the Social Security Administration (SSA). The average for women is $1,872.43, creating a gender gap of $409.85 per month.

It has been revealed that the gap is visible the moment workers become eligible for benefits. At age 62, men receive an average of $1,572.83 per month while women receive $1,285.50. This difference of nearly $300 a month persists and grows as retirees age.

According to recent reports, the figures in the table below represent snapshots of everyone at a specific age today, regardless of when they first claimed. Your own benefit depends on your work history and when you choose to start your checks. Full retirement age (FRA) ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later.

The data above is as of December 2025 and comes from the SSA's retired-worker records.

The higher male average reflects historical differences in lifetime earnings and years spent in the paid workforce. The SSA calculates your benefit based on your average wages across your 35 highest-earning years, adjusted for inflation and run through the primary insurance amount (PIA) formula.

Recent findings suggest that longevity affects how long these checks last. A man who is 65 today is expected to live about 18 more years, while a woman of the same age is expected to live about 21 more years, according to the SSA.

Recent findings suggest that social Security is designed to replace only about 40% of pre-retirement income. This share is well short of what most retirees need to cover their costs, so many rely on savings or other income sources.

According to recent reports, annual cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs) are designed to help these checks keep pace with inflation, though they often fall short. The 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment that will take effect in 2027 will add about $91 per month to the $2,529.62 average for 70-year-old men.

Married men may be able to help their spouses get more from Social Security through spousal or survivor benefits. Once you claim your retirement benefit, your spouse becomes eligible to claim a spousal benefit, worth up to one-half of the amount you qualify for at your FRA, provided they're at least 62 at the time. They will only receive this amount if it's worth more than their own retirement benefit.

After you pass away, your spouse will become eligible for a survivor benefit, worth up to 100% of the amount you were receiving or eligible for at the time of your death. This can be a significant help to them, especially if you don't have a ton of personal savings.

For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • Industry observers note that the latest Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone owners in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

Industry observers note that the latest Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app users on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

Sources indicate that there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

Recent findings suggest that one of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

According to recent reports, the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

It has been revealed that along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google announced AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1073 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1073 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • Latest data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • It has been revealed that also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

Latest data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

It has been revealed that also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

According to recent reports, employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

“As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

Industry observers note that the report shows how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse said, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Sources indicate that greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

In a recent development, what we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson mentioned Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he remarked.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ fresh top stressor.

It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

Industry observers note that “The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report shows 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the manufacturer, human or AI,” Samson said. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

Samson stated that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

Recent findings suggest that “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson said. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most key decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse mentioned.

Sources indicate that A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more crucial tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse stated.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson stated. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you use an AI chatbot and you’re concerned about your privacy and the personal information it ingests, you can do something about it.
  • Luckily, you can mitigate or even eliminate the amount of data Claude knows about you, as long as you know where to look.
  • From having Claude train on your conversations to track your location and more, here are a series of settings you should consider changing if you want to stay on top of your privacy when using one of the best AI chatbots around.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you use an AI chatbot and you’re concerned about your privacy and the personal information it ingests, you can do something about it. While Claude — our top pick for AI chatbots — is one of the better options when it comes to privacy, the default settings can still leave something to be desired if you value yours.

Luckily, you can mitigate or even eliminate the amount of data Claude knows about you, as long as you know where to look.

From having Claude train on your conversations to track your location and more, here are a series of settings you should consider changing if you want to stay on top of your privacy when using one of the best AI chatbots around.

Industry observers note that by default, most AI chatbots have a setting on by default that allows them to be trained on the conversations you have. This is the first and likely the most notable setting you need to disable. Here’s how to turn it off.

The settings essentially remain the same across web, iOS and Android:.

It has been revealed that you may not see this option because with some accounts, like Enterprise plans, Claude doesn’t automatically collect this data. So if you have a Claude account through work, you might not have to worry about this.

While you’re at it, if you’re a Claude Code user, these settings will let you delete Code sessions stored on Anthropic’s server without deleting local sessions on your computer.

If you’ve ever shared a chat with anyone, you can also delete those chats in this menu as well.

Read More: Keep Your Data Yours: How to Opt Out of AI Chatbot Training.

Sources indicate that anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. How you go about doing this will depend on what device you’re using to access Claude.

In a recent development, according to the support article, if you’re using the mobile app (iOS or Android) or the web extension, the location settings are located within the device’s settings and not the Claude app settings. However, I found two ways to do this on Android. (See below.).

The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

However, if you already have given Claude access on Android or iOS, here’s how you can revoke permission.

I was surprised to see a section in the Settings of the Android app that I didn’t see on iOS, but it will also allow you to disable your location right from the app.

One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

Like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

It has been revealed that if you’d prefer a clean slate, you can ask in the chat what memories it has collected about you and then tell Claude to delete specific memories or all of them. However, there’s a dedicated section in the settings to help you view and manage memories directly.

In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:.

This will display all stored memories Claude has for you. You can edit a specific memory to your liking by clicking on the pencil icon on the right side of the memory or delete it entirely by clicking on the trash icon.

To prevent Claude from creating fresh memories from your conversations:.

Recent findings suggest that if you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

According to recent reports, however, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero.
  • The thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use.
  • Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

The thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

It could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

This is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

In a recent development, the reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this new platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

The Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

Recent findings suggest that keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also notes on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

Meta’s Carbon Emissions Went Up 45% Last Year. AI Is Making It Worse

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used.
  • In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the tech giant is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.
  • It’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Substantial Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the tech giant is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.

It’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, mentioned in 2023 that the firm’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”.

It has been revealed that meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the company says. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

It has been revealed that take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its new data center designs compared to its original ones.

It has been revealed that but, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The company also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”.

Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

Your Google AI mode searches can stay private now with ‘temporary threads’ – here’s how

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends.
  • Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.
  • Recent findings suggest that new to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

Recent findings suggest that new to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

This option is currently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Sources indicate that try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

Hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a latest thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s new Skills.

Industry observers note that certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google claims:.

It has been revealed that “Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google said on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

In a recent development, google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

For those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

Sources indicate that I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google announced that it would be rolling out new settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

#73886. Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (609 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (609 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message.
  • Recent findings suggest that the privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a latest default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data.
  • That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

Recent findings suggest that the privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a latest default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data. In a blog post announcing the change, Signal President Meredith Whittaker stated these AI bots scan what’s on your screen to get to know you, capturing your data and making it available to AI systems to fulfill your requests, such as answering questions you may ask.

That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote. So it’s putting a stop to it with a default setting to block screenshots in the Signal app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants try to capture information on Android screens by default.

Whittaker said that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

Now the tech giant is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

The problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal claims that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

“Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,” Whittaker wrote.

It has been revealed that whittaker said the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how major tech AI agents work.

It has been revealed that “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker remarked. “This is also the reason we are at the moment unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”.

In most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

It has been revealed that “So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” remarked Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”.

If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

Strand said the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

“They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand said.

Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure manufacturer Oracle (ORCL) recently announced better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

After hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he noted.

Industry observers note that "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," stated DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as fresh contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

It has been revealed that diFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

"RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," mentioned Gesuale.

The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space company with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst stated, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

Gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

"Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," stated Anmuth.

In a recent development, in the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst said. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

Meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst stated. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

In a recent development, so too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this new take on the OS is the epitome of that.

The distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with latest ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

In a recent development, the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

It has been revealed that if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

It has been revealed that pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a newly introduced workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

Another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

In a recent development, once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

As I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One issue that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI upgrade system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

In a recent development, I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an revision component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

According to recent reports, you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my new favorite free productivity suite.

It has been revealed that pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

#73881. Latest Update: Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (753 w)
📖 Baca

Latest Update: Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (753 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars.
  • In a recent development, it’s an exciting time for NASA.
  • Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

In a recent development, it’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other big win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

These satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the debut of Blue Origin’s Upcoming Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the firm was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

It has been revealed that escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their latest trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally indicates up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA indicates that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

It has been revealed that by the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally released Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and rolled out themselves into outer space.

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a upcoming strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, noted in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”.

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.
