Industry News: I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1639 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
  • According to recent reports, take Southwest Airlines, for example.
  • Sources indicate that "Experiences create lifetime memories,” indicates Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

According to recent reports, take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

Sources indicate that "Experiences create lifetime memories,” indicates Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

Southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but significant-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

The event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

Even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

As of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

It has been revealed that $1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

According to recent reports, four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

If you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

Industry observers note that using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

It has been revealed that daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

Ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

According to recent reports, again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

Sources indicate that I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

Grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

Industry observers note that the biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

You’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

Sources indicate that with that mentioned, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

Scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

Finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

In a recent development, but every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

According to recent reports, personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

"We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” notes Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other owners.

According to recent reports, also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse noted the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing customers’ private data,” Reuters noted.

Reuters said “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she remarked she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

Sources indicate that similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

These are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

As a company, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

Sources indicate that public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if customers believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

Signal to restrict screenshots over AI agent concerns – again

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots.
  • Sources indicate that whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers.
  • Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set new limits on screenshots. The company will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

Sources indicate that whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

According to recent reports, “Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker stated. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

Signal’s move is another reminder of how Big Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

In a recent development, just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

Signal noted its protections don’t currently work on MacOS.

In a recent development, “It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

“Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker said.

What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
  • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
  • You don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The big day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

You don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, indicates Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

It has been revealed that non-electronic toys are a good bet, says Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

According to recent reports, neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold says.

While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

“Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” states Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley says.

Got some counter space and an itch for a new food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

“Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath states. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold says.

Electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath says.

Sources indicate that gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath notes. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

That said, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold indicates.

According to recent reports, for best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, claims consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after Fresh Year’s Day.

“Significant-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold states.

In a recent development, many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

In a recent development, shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold notes. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

It has been revealed that just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath says. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

One caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch states. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

Fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch indicates.

Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a upcoming customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

Let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch claims. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

Sources indicate that check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley says. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

Recent findings suggest that use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people new tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.
  • Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches.
  • Sources indicate that AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people new tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches. Meta’s Muse AI agent quietly builds a profile on you the second you start using it, even if you explicitly tell it not to. That turns Jolly, its supposedly cute and cuddly mascot, into the friendly face of some serious security flaws.

Sources indicate that AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf. But the trade-off is privacy and control. You’re handing over your personal information to a black box with little visibility into how it’s used. Multiple incidents are fueling a conversation about the dangers of agentic AI and whether they require higher security standards before being granted access to user data.

That’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

It has been revealed that given Meta’s track record of privacy fines, data sharing and security challenges, it’s worth proceeding with caution. A few months ago, a lifestyle blogger reported that the social media platform’s AI asked intrusive questions about her kids and pieced together private information about her life from her posts. Meta’s controversial smart glasses have received pushback on multiple fronts — from its facial recognition software to the way it captures and stores data.

Despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

Industry observers note that muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

Sources indicate that within weeks of launch earlier this fall, a security researcher demonstrated that the assistant could be hijacked via a zero-day exploit that Meta’s own documentation acknowledged was easy to trigger. Then, an investigative journalist discovered Muse digging through his private Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed the claim, but Apple took it seriously enough to roll out an emergency upgrade to MacOS privacy controls.

More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse owners, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

If the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

Recent findings suggest that muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report reveals that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

Muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta launched the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the company planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

According to recent reports, muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN firm Surfshark said it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

  • If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.

If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current consumers will lose access to both next year.

According to recent reports, all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

The change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”.

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

In a recent development, google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

According to recent reports, as part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

Google says that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app. Part of the goal is to give owners the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

According to recent reports, the other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the company starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

Industry observers note that google says Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and customers will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Recent findings suggest that gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google confirmed earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Users in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

Industry observers note that on your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

According to recent reports, clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a upcoming page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. Another newly introduced feature, as revealed by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which indicates your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:.

Stein noted the fresh sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.

“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

Still, for Google specifically, you can go to Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity to turn off AI training.

It has been revealed that google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google declared several other latest AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion users in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the organization’s “fastest growing product ever.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Moon is now a few days past its First Quarter phase, and we're well into the Waxing Gibbous stage, which means each night, a little more of its surface is illuminated. This pattern will continue until we reach the Full Moon.

According to recent reports, as of Friday, Nov. 20, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 77% of its surface visible.

Industry observers note that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis and Tranquillitatis, as well as the Kepler Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Posidonius Crater, the Clavius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11, 14, and 17 landing spots.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

Sources indicate that according to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a Newly introduced Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Sources indicate that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that hyundai pulled back the cover on the latest 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class.
  • Sources indicate that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand.
  • The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hyundai pulled back the cover on the latest 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

Sources indicate that the humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an important one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

The updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

In a recent development, an updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a new Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

According to recent reports, sharing the stage in LA, the fresh nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

Inside, a new cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

Pleos Connect, Hyundai’s latest Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

According to recent reports, the Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s fresh AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai notes the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

“Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” said Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the newly introduced Elantra is anything but bland.

In a recent development, the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent new SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

Sources indicate that the sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai says the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

Industry observers note that hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

Recent findings suggest that editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Asked on Reddit: I Lost My Job; What Should I Do First?

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.
  • Industry observers note that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty?
  • Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

Industry observers note that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any big moves, indicates Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

That’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he claims. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, says John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a latest policy in the health insurance marketplace.

Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your new job search — is also an crucial part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty says.

“Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

At the same time, it’s vital to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage company, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a newly introduced park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

“Having that release is mentally a significant thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he states. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, says Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

In a recent development, people often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she says.

Starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine indicates. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

Doing something newly introduced also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so plan accordingly.

Sources indicate that all three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

The Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

In a recent development, reddit is an online forum where consumers share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Dave Kovaleski – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:23PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nu Holdings ›.

These are interesting times, with Congressional upheaval in the United States amid an uncertain economic environment with rising interest rates, elevated inflation, and potentially slowing economic growth.

It is typically not a great combination for most financial sector stocks, as the sector often serves as an economic bellwether and thrives when the economy is strong. The S&P 500 financials sector has returned just 2.7% year-to-date, which is among the worst performers among sectors.

According to recent reports, many financial stocks have tumbled in recent weeks, caught up in the Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 sell-off over the past month. Here are two financial stocks that are at or near 52-week lows that are good long-term buys, even amid the lackluster outlook for the sector in 2027.

Nu Holdings (NU -4.65%) is the parent firm of Nubank, a Brazil-based bank and financial firm. Nu stock is down 28% year-to-date, but most of that has come in the past month, when the stock has plummeted 17% to its current $11.95 per share, which is hovering near a 52-week low.

The reason for the swoon is almost entirely due to the results of the presidential election in October, where the liberal incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva beat the conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro in a surprise victory.

Most Brazilian stocks tanked after the Lula victory, as the challenger was seen as a better option to spur Brazil's economic growth. But Lula has been in office for three terms already, a time when Nu has been growing like a weed, so it seems like more of a knee-jerk reaction than anything to do with Nu's business model or prospects.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that for investors, it is a tremendous opportunity to buy the dip on this valuation reset. Nu stock is trading at just 11 times forward earnings and has a minuscule five-year P/E-to-growth (PEG) ratio of 0.13, suggesting it is well undervalued relative to its long-term earnings.

While Nu is the largest bank in Brazil, the low-overhead digital bank has expanded into Mexico and Colombia. And in September, it introduced in the United States. Its growth has been impressive, as in the most recent quarter, revenue rose 37% year over year to a record $6.3 billion, gross profit jumped 35% to $2.6 billion, and net income climbed 31% to a record $1.1 billion.

Nu added 3.7 million customers in Q3, bringing its total to 143 million globally. It has grown rapidly outside of Brazil, and the U.S. launch offers a longer-term growth opportunity as the U.S. build-out is expected to take 12 to 30 months.

Sources indicate that fidelity National Financial (FNF +0.97%) is a leading provider of title insurance for the real estate market. So, it has struggled in recent years as home sales and refinancings have plummeted due to high interest rates and inflation. And the outlook doesn't look much better in 2027, with perhaps a gradual recovery potentially coming in 2028.

It has been revealed that fidelity National stock is down about 22% year to date and is not far from its 52-week low, trading at around $42.60 per share. Its 52-week low came in late October at around $37 per share.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In a recent development, but here are a few reasons why I like Fidelity National right now, despite the weak outlook for real estate. For one, the stock is trading at just 11 times earnings, which is the lowest it has been in four years. But the firm has been resilient during a difficult market.

Revenue dropped about 10% last quarter to $3.6 billion, mostly due to the loss of revenue from the sale of its reinsurance business, which was undertaken to improve cash flow and strengthen the balance sheet. The capital from the reinsurance business will be used to invest in core areas. The title segment actually saw revenue increase year over year to $2.4 billion from $2.3 billion.

It has been revealed that secondly, Fidelity National holds a majority stake in a secondary business, F&G Annuities & Life (FG -0.05%). This business had a strong quarter, excluding the sale of the reinsurance business, with assets before reinsurance rising 7% to $76 billion. Further, its total core sales in this segment rose about 5% to $2.3 billion in the quarter, driven by annuity sales.

This business should sustain Fidelity National during periods of high interest rates and sluggish real estate sales because higher interest rates translate to higher annuity rates and higher spreads. That, in turn, leads to more sales.

Industry observers note that the other piece that makes Fidelity National attractive is its excellent high-yield dividend. In Q3, it boosted its dividend 4% to $0.54 per share, marking the 15th consecutive year of dividend increases. Further, it offers a yield of 4.98% and a payout ratio of just 41%, suggesting the dividend is safe.

Analysts rate FNF as an overwhelming buy, with a median price target of $55 per share, indicating 28% upside.

Neocloud company CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

According to recent reports, recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

In a recent development, chatterjee mentioned CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

Recent findings suggest that "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," noted Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

Chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

It has been revealed that after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

Sources indicate that over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and new markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security manufacturer, Powell said. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

Meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell noted.

BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

Powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

It has been revealed that in a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he said.

Devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

Sources indicate that overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the manufacturer if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he stated. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

"Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," said Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    #73856. With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (766 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (766 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
    • The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
    • A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

    The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

    A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

    One bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

    Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

    Right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) indicated consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

    While CPI highlights how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

    To cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

    Recent findings suggest that even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how quickly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

    Recent findings suggest that if you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

    But newly introduced data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

    Pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

    “Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun remarked in a news release.

    Whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

    Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

    Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

    Think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

    Spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

    Addas a preferred source on Google.

    • Could USA Rare Earth (USAR -8.73%) be the right stock to put your money in right now?
    • According to recent reports, USA Rare Earth is a rare-earth mining company that wants to become a mine-to-magnet company.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Steven Porrello – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than USA Rare Earth ›.

    As of this writing on Nov. 19, the S&P 500 is tanking; indeed, the index is on track to notch its sixth consecutive day of losses. A few days ago, Nvidia's blockbuster earnings came and went without confetti -- or former CEO Jensen Huang. Widespread apprehension seems to pervade every nook and cranny of the stock market, as the uncertain future of artificial intelligence (AI) hangs over everything.

    So what about mining stocks? What about rare-earths? We still need critical minerals. Could USA Rare Earth (USAR -8.73%) be the right stock to put your money in right now?

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, USA Rare Earth is a rare-earth mining company that wants to become a mine-to-magnet company. Its flagship mining project -- the Round Top deposit in Texas -- is currently under development, but its recent acquisition of the Brazilian mine Serra Verde means that USA Rare Earth is now an actual miner.

    Production at Serra Verde began in 2024, and in October 2026, the mine began shipping rare-earth materials to a U.S. government-backed buyer under a 15-year purchasing agreement.

    Those shipments have given USA Rare Earth something that many early-stage miners need badly: revenue. Still, it's nothing to write home about. Last quarter, USA Rare Earth generated about $3 million, notably missing Wall Street's expectations of $6.5 million. Worse, it reported an operating loss of about $141 million and an adjusted loss of $0.44 per share, more than double the $0.19 loss analysts expected.

    In today's market, with several macroeconomic headwinds blowing together, I want to encourage a cautious approach to USA Rare Earth.

    In a recent development, there's no question in my mind that rare-earth metals will be valuable in the future. We have plenty of uses for them, and their scarcity has many governments concerned. But that doesn't mean every rare-earth mining manufacturer will be a winner on Wall Street, and for USA Rare Earth, two risks need to be considered.

    The first is that Round Top Deposit, its flagship project, is still in the exploration phase: Its commercial viability has not been determined. Even more concerning is the fact that miners have been trying to develop Round Top for decades without commercial success. Its history stretches back to the 1970s, when it was investigated for fluorite, and the asset has changed hands several times before coming under USA Rare Earth's control.

    Recent findings suggest that the second risk to consider is rising interest rates. Even if Round Top proves economically valuable beyond the market's wildest dreams, USA Rare Earth will need substantial capital to bring the mine into production. Higher interest rates would make borrowing more expensive, likely forcing the firm to concern more shares and dilute existing investors.

    Between these risks and USA Rare Earth's mounting losses, I see more reasons to avoid this stock than to buy it right now.

    Breaking: Micron Stock Just Hit Its Lowest Price Since May. I'd Buy More Now.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Shares of Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) fell about 14% on Friday to close near $595.
    • Micron closed at a record high of $1,213.56 on June 25, so the stock has lost about half its value over five months.
    • It has been revealed that but management noted in late September that customers had already committed to over three-quarters of Micron's planned shipments for this fiscal year.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 21, 2026 at 3:52PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›.

    Shares of Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) fell about 14% on Friday to close near $595. That's the lowest close for the memory chipmaker's stock since early May.

    Micron closed at a record high of $1,213.56 on June 25, so the stock has lost about half its value over five months. And memory stocks dropped across the board on Friday, with Sandisk down about 16%.

    It has been revealed that but management noted in late September that customers had already committed to over three-quarters of Micron's planned shipments for this fiscal year. At roughly $595, the stock costs about 3.5 times expected earnings for that year, fiscal 2027, which ends in early September 2027.

    I think the fall has more to do with worries over memory prices than with how much Micron can sell.

    Micron president and chief operating officer Manish Bhatia noted on the organization's Sept. 30 earnings call that "we have more than 75% of our shipments committed for the year," referring to fiscal 2027. He added that this "allows us to shift our conversations on allocation with our customers out to 2028.".

    Put another way, buyers have mostly claimed their share of Micron's output through next September, and the talks have already moved on.

    Recent findings suggest that the numbers back that up, helped by demand from artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. Micron's revenue in its fiscal fourth quarter, the 14 weeks ending Sept. 3, came to $54.2 billion. That was 31% higher than in the previous quarter and 379% above the year-ago quarter. Earnings per share climbed more than elevenfold year over year, to $32.87. For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, management sees revenue of about $61.5 billion, roughly 13% above fiscal Q4, and it expects every quarter of the year to beat the one before.

    Sources indicate that so growth is easing from a blistering pace. But it isn't reversing.

    Committed shipments, though, don't all come with committed prices. Micron's multiyear strategic customer agreements, which it estimates will make up over 35% of its revenue through 2030, are where it sets most prices ahead of time. Even in those deals, around a quarter of the expected revenue is priced periodically based on market prices.

    Industry observers note that that probably leaves most of Micron's sales linked to where memory prices head. And prices did a lot of the work last quarter.

    In fiscal Q4, prices for Micron's DRAM (the short-term memory in servers, PCs, and phones) rose a high-teens percentage from the previous quarter. DRAM made up 73% of revenue. Prices for its NAND flash storage chips, 26% of revenue, climbed around 30%.

    Recent findings suggest that these price gains show in Micron's gross margin under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). It was 44.7% a year before, reached 84.6% by fiscal Q3, then hit 86.8% in fiscal Q4. Management's forecast for this quarter is around 86%. It expects margins to inch up over the rest of fiscal 2027, though with "a more moderate rate of price increases.".

    There are early signs prices might ease. On Nov. 19, TrendForce predicted that NAND flash contract prices may drop 0% to 5% in the first quarter of 2027, with a broader downturn starting in the second quarter. Also, TrendForce said the average spot price for mainstream DDR4 memory chips dipped around 1% in the week ending Nov. 17, while branded DDR5 spot prices were mostly steady.

    Sources indicate that sure, a 1% dip in spot prices isn't a memory bust. But I'd track DRAM prices closely from here. After all, Micron's profits have ridden on rising prices.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that micron has plenty of room before lower prices erase its profits. The cost of the chips Micron sold was just around 13% of its revenue in fiscal Q4. Rough math demonstrates that if prices dropped 30% and these costs stayed flat, its gross margin would still be about 81%. That would be around where it was for all of fiscal 2026, and about double fiscal 2025's 39.8%.

    It has been revealed that of course, prices might drop more than that. And costs won't stand still while Micron keeps building. Its capital expenditures came to about $27.4 billion in fiscal 2026, almost double the year before.

    According to recent reports, but the stock price already allows for a steep fall in profits. Even on fiscal 2026's results, when Micron earned $74.33 per share, the stock costs just around 8 times earnings. On this year's expected earnings, it's under half that.

    Industry observers note that I'd buy more here, albeit only if the position is still small even after my addition, and I'd keep Micron a small part of a diversified portfolio. Memory prices can turn fast, and the stock might drop further before they do.
