    This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1478 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, hilton is making a massive play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, hilton is making a massive play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    Room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    It has been revealed that if you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    Recent findings suggest that you can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    According to recent reports, make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    It has been revealed that for cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    In a recent development, I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    For lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    It has been revealed that you can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    For a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    Industry observers note that one of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    Next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    One of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    If you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    Verizon Pays Out $11.7 Billion a Year in Dividends. Here’s the Free Cash Flow Math Behind Its 6.2%-Yielding Payout.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Verizon Communications ›.
    • Sources indicate that verizon (VZ +1.62%) pays $0.7075 per share in dividends to its investors each quarter.
    • Here's a look at the free cash flow that supports its high-yielding dividend.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Matt DiLallo – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:03PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Verizon Communications ›.

    Sources indicate that verizon (VZ +1.62%) pays $0.7075 per share in dividends to its investors each quarter. At its recent share price, the telecom giant yields 6.2%, significantly higher than the S&P 500's 1.1%. Verizon's dividend costs about $2.9 billion per quarter, or around $11.7 billion annually.

    Here's a look at the free cash flow that supports its high-yielding dividend.

    Verizon generates substantial recurring revenue as customers pay their internet and broadband bills. It hauled in $34.3 billion of revenue during the third quarter, up 1.5% year over year. It has generated $103 billion of revenue during the first nine months of this year (up 1.2%).

    The company converts a significant portion of its revenue into cash flow. Verizon generated $29.9 billion of cash flow from operations during the first nine months of this year, up nearly 7% compared to the year-ago period. The telecom giant spent $11.9 billion on capital expenditures to maintain and expand its networks, leaving it with $18 billion in free cash flow. That's up from $15.8 billion compared to the prior-year period. It was more than enough to cover the $8.8 billion Verizon paid in dividends. The company used its excess free cash flow to repurchase $4 billion of shares and strengthen its balance sheet.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Verizon presently expects to spend $16 billion to $16.5 billion on capital expenditures this year, down from $17 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, it now expects its free cash flow to increase by as much as 12% from last year's $20.1 billion, implying roughly $22.5 billion. That will cover its $11.7 billion in dividends nearly two times over.

    That gives Verizon plenty of room to grow its dividend. The manufacturer delivered its 20th consecutive annual dividend increase earlier this year. It has been growing its payout at a modest low-single-digit rate, which should continue. That would still leave it with ample excess free cash flow to repurchase shares while continuing to strengthen its balance sheet. Verizon's debt has increased by $20 billion over the past year due to its acquisition of Frontier. However, it has a reasonable 2.3x leverage ratio (up from 2.2x in the year-ago period) and solid credit ratings (A-/BBB+/Baa1).

    At over 6%, Verizon has one of the highest dividend yields in the S&P 500. However, it's not a high-risk dividend stock. The firm comfortably covers its payout with cash, providing it with excess to strengthen its already solid balance sheet and repurchase shares. While Verizon won't provide much growth, it can certainly provide investors with a lucrative, steadily rising stream of passive dividend income.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:23PM EST.
    • Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%) have fallen roughly 60% from their all-time highs in June 2026.
    • In a recent development, benjamin Graham, the man who helped train Wall Street icon Warren Buffett, liked to say that Wall Street was a voting machine in the short term and a weighing machine in the long term.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Rocket Lab ›.

    Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB -10.92%) have fallen roughly 60% from their all-time highs in June 2026. That's a massive decline. And yet, even with that decline, a $10,000 investment in the stock five years ago would still be worth more than $33,000 as of this writing. There's an important backstory here, even as Space Exploration Corporation (SPCX -7.69%) makes the biggest headlines in the still-emerging space industry. Here's what you need to know.

    In a recent development, benjamin Graham, the man who helped train Wall Street icon Warren Buffett, liked to say that Wall Street was a voting machine in the short term and a weighing machine in the long term. The point here is that emotions are what move stock prices in the near term, while business success is recognized over the long term. Graham and Buffett both used this insight to highlight value investments, but it is equally notable when considering growth stocks, assuming you have a long enough investment horizon.

    That fact is on clear display in the space industry. There was massive enthusiasm for space-related stocks leading up to SpaceX's initial public offering (IPO). That enthusiasm petered out after the IPO. That's not particularly shocking, given the hype on Wall Street and Main Street around that IPO. Rocket Lab simply got caught up in the emotional swing since it is a SpaceX competitor. But that doesn't mean Rocket Lab isn't achieving success as a business.

    Recent news was flooded with results from SpaceX's Starship launch. On the negative side, the tech giant failed to catch the spaceship's lower section (the booster rocket). On the positive side, it successfully caught the upper portion (the actual spacecraft). The end goal is to have a completely reusable rocket system, which would dramatically reduce the cost of getting to space. It is very exciting stuff.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In the shadow of this industry leader, Rocket Lab achieved its own milestone on Nov. 14, 2026. That was the day the manufacturer marked the 100th launch of its Electron spacecraft. The company noted in a press release that it had set "a new record for reaching 100 releases faster than any other commercially developed rocket." SpaceX gets most of the headlines, but Rocket Lab is making progress as a business, too.

    In a recent development, to be fair, Rocket Lab is a money-losing start-up. So it isn't an appropriate investment for risk-averse investors. But it may be of interest to growth investors that have a long-term focus. The space industry is still in its early stages of development. SpaceX is the dominant player, but there will be room for more than one manufacturer.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    That's been highlighted recently by SpaceX's own satellite launch aims, which are limiting other companies' access to its releases. If the tech giant increasingly focuses on its own business, it leaves companies with no other option but to turn to competitors like Rocket Lab. And given the success Rocket Lab has had with its own launches, investors are clearly recognizing the long-term opportunity even as emotional investors create material price volatility. That's why the stock is up so much over the long term but down so much over the short term.

    In a recent development, rocket Lab isn't for the faint of heart, given that the stock is likely to remain volatile. And operating in the shadow of SpaceX won't help the situation any. However, Rocket Lab is making vital progress as a business. Over the long term, assuming you can handle the volatility, it could be an attractive option in the still-emerging space industry.

    Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

    In a recent development, high-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

    According to recent reports, the high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

    Spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

    Sources indicate that the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

    Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," remarked Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

    It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

    Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

    "The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone noted.

    He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

    That mentioned, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

    Industry observers note that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

    While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

    In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, mentioned Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

    Industry observers note that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

    Recent findings suggest that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, remarked Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

    The overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

    Industry observers note that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

    The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

    Sources indicate that "It is isolated," she mentioned. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

    For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

    "We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she said.

    Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

    According to recent reports, but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

    "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin said. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

    It's also vital to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, stated R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

    "With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

    High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

    Sources indicate that "That's when spreads really widen out," he stated. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

Also, a potential margin improvement should help Nvidia deliver strong earnings growth next year, which could send the stock soaring.

    College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1373 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
    • According to recent reports, before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
    • Recent findings suggest that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

    According to recent reports, before you go searching for a scholarship, it's notable to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

    Recent findings suggest that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

    Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

    Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

    Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

    Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

    Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

    Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

    These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

    Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s key to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

    Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

    Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

    Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

    Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

    In a recent development, some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

    Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

    Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

    Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

    Sources indicate that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

    Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

    Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

    Scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

    It has been revealed that which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

    Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

    Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

    Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

    The best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

    Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

    Industry observers note that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

    Recent findings suggest that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a massive impact when you add several of them together.

    Recent findings suggest that understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

    According to recent reports, not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    Is Tilray a Buy at Its Record Low, or Is It a Value Trap?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:51PM EST.
    • The cannabis industry has been a massive disappointment in recent years, and even most industry leaders haven't escaped the bloodbath.
    • Recent findings suggest that tilray Brands faces a difficult regulatory landscape in the cannabis market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 21, 2026 at 4:51PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Tilray Brands ›.

    The cannabis industry has been a massive disappointment in recent years, and even most industry leaders haven't escaped the bloodbath. Take, for instance, Tilray Brands (TLRY -8.70%), one of the largest players in the Canadian cannabis market. Tilray has significantly underperformed the broader market over the past half-decade, losing more than 90% of its value. The tech giant is now near record lows. Is Tilray stock a buy at current levels, or would investors be catching a falling knife?

    Recent findings suggest that tilray Brands faces a difficult regulatory landscape in the cannabis market. Recreational use of the substance remains illegal at the federal level in the U.S. It is legal in Canada, where the company is headquartered, but that market has its own challenges.

    Obtaining the proper licenses in Canada is a complex and time-consuming process. The market north of the border is also characterized by stiff competition and persistent supply gluts. Although Tilray is an industry leader, these problems have harmed its financial results. The manufacturer has diversified its business in response.

    It now operates four segments: cannabis, beverage, wellness (which offers a variety of products, including hemp-based foods), and distribution (which focuses on selling pharmaceutical products in certain international markets). But even a more diversified pool of operations has done little to improve Tilray's financial results.

    Sources indicate that in the first quarter of its fiscal year 2027, which ended on Aug. 31, Tilray's revenue increased by 23% year over year to a record $257 million. That looks impressive at first glance, but Tilray's top line did not grow that much organically. Earlier this year, it acquired certain assets associated with BrewDog, a craft brewery based in the United Kingdom.

    Industry observers note that this acquisition added $55.9 million in revenue to the company's total for the period. If we subtract that from Tilray's total revenue, its top line comes in at $201.2 million for the period, down about 4% year over year.

    This includes cannabis revenue of $56.1 million, which dropped 13% year over year. Wellness revenue stayed roughly flat at $15.3 million, while distribution revenue was $84.3 million, 14% higher than the year-ago period. Beverage revenue minus the BrewDog acquisition declined 18% year over year to $45.6 million.

    According to recent reports, so of Tilray's four business segments, only one posted strong year-over-year organic sales growth. Meanwhile, the firm's operating loss was $24.1 million, compared with $2.1 million in operating income in the year-ago period. It also turned in a net loss per share of $0.32, after breaking even in the comparable period of the previous fiscal year.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Industry observers note that tilray's poor financial results aren't the only problem. The company also faces a highly uncertain future, even given recent regulatory progress in the U.S. The federal government reclassified certain medical cannabis products and has discussed broader reclassification, which could encompass recreational cannabis.

    But the substance remains illegal at the federal level. That means it still cannot be transported across state lines, among other restrictions. So, Tilray's opportunities in the U.S. remain severely limited. Will that change anytime soon? It's hard to say. Nobody knows if or when the U.S. will legalize recreational use of cannabis at the federal level.

    Sources indicate that even if it does, Tilray might face problems similar to those it faced in Canada. What about other countries? Could Tilray bounce back by tapping into international markets? Unfortunately, that also seems unlikely. For instance, Germany legalized recreational cannabis in 2024, but this did very little to boost Tilray's results, despite the manufacturer's presence in the country.

    Germany allowed people to grow cannabis at home (within certain limits) or join non-commercial cannabis clubs. The law left little room for commercial companies like Tilray. So, the pot grower faces a stringent regulatory environment practically wherever it goes, and that might not change anytime soon. Tilray is unlikely to bounce back.

    Investing in the stock, even at its record low, isn't worth the trouble.

    Defense Stocks Fell After the Midterms. Here’s the 1 Defense Name I’d Buy Anyway -- and Why It Isn’t Lockheed Martin.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The midterm election results sent a shudder through the defense industry.
    • It has been revealed that president Donald Trump is proposing a $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027, but time is running out to pass the budget in a lame-duck Congress.
    • It has been revealed that RTX (RTX -1.32%) is one of only two major U.S.-based defense stocks whose shares have risen since the midterm elections.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By James Halley – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than RTX ›.

    The midterm election results sent a shudder through the defense industry.

    It has been revealed that president Donald Trump is proposing a $1.5 trillion defense budget for 2027, but time is running out to pass the budget in a lame-duck Congress. Next year's Congress is likely to take a more critical look at defense spending.

    It has been revealed that RTX (RTX -1.32%) is one of only two major U.S.-based defense stocks whose shares have risen since the midterm elections. There are four reasons why RTX is the one defense stock I'd buy over Lockheed Martin (LMT -1.11%).

    Unlike many of its peers, the company is positioned to continue doing well because its revenue streams also include sales of parts and equipment to commercial airlines, providing a cushion if next year's Congress slashes the defense budget.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that RTX has three segments, but only one of them is a pure-play defense segment: Raytheon, which makes air and missile defense systems. The other two segments, Pratt & Whitney and Collins Aerospace, make defense and commercial airline products. Pratt & Whitney makes aircraft engines for civilian and military aircraft, while its Collins Aerospace segment makes aircraft systems, including avionics, navigation systems, and flight controls for commercial and defense aircraft.

    Sources indicate that lockheed Martin's shares, on the other hand, are down more than 3% since the elections because it has little commercial sales, with more than 69% of its revenue coming from the U.S. government.

    Industry observers note that RTX reported double-digit revenue and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) growth in the third quarter. Revenue was reported as $25 billion, up 11% year over year, and adjusted EPS grew by 33% over the prior year to $2.26. The organization also raised full-year guidance. It says it expects 2026 sales of $97 billion to $97.5 billion, up from earlier estimates of between $95 billion and $96 billion. It also raised adjusted EPS from $7.10 to $7.25, up to $7.65–$7.75.

    Adjusted segment operating margins expanded by 310 basis points in the third quarter, and because aircraft engine maintenance and spare parts carry higher profit margins than initial equipment sales, RTX's installed base of commercial engines and avionics acts as a compounding cash-flow machine independent of Capitol Hill.

    Pratt & Whitney's commercial aftermarket sales jumped 21% year over year, while Collins Aerospace's adjusted operating profit surged 50%.

    Lockheed Martin also had a strong quarter, with revenue rising 11% year over year, to $20.7 billion and EPS of $7.97, up 14% from the same period last year. However, because so much of its revenue lately is tied to Iran war spending, that could slow at any time.

    RTX reported a backlog of $340 billion in the third quarter, including $164 billion in defense sales and $176 billion in commercial sales. That provides a great deal of stability for investors looking at the manufacturer's long-term potential, as it represents three years' worth of revenue.

    According to recent reports, just in the third quarter, Raytheon booked nearly $59 billion in defense awards, including production contracts for Tomahawk missiles and air-to-air missiles. Even with Democrats soon to control Congress, global demand for air defense and munitions makes these multiyear contracts highly resilient.

    Lockheed Martin's backlog is smaller at $292 billion, and all of that is tied to defense contracts.

    According to recent reports, the company raised its quarterly dividend by 7.4% this year to $0.73 per share, the 32nd consecutive year it has increased its dividend. The dividend yield is an above-average 1.42%, and while that's lower than Lockheed Martin's 2.39% yield, RTX's streak of raising dividends is eight years longer.

    In addition, over the past three years, RTX has increased its dividend by more than 23%, while Lockheed has raised its dividend by just over 9%.

    RTX stands out as a stronger buy than Lockheed Martin right now largely because its balanced business model insulates it from post-midterm political turbulence on Capitol Hill.

    RTX's greater commercial footprint not only provides a steady buffer against congressional scrutiny, but also fuels a high-margin aftermarket engine and spare-parts business that acts as a compounding cash-flow engine independent of Pentagon appropriations.

    Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

    Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

    Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

    According to recent reports, the five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the tech giant's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

    In a recent development, furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the firm's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

    In a recent development, wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

    Sources indicate that wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it reveals its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

    Industry observers note that heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

    Recent findings suggest that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

    Recent findings suggest that "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," remarked the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

    While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the manufacturer's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

    Sources indicate that morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

    Next is semiconductor manufacturer Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

    After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

    According to recent reports, the five-star analyst remarked that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

    In a recent development, while XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

    Svanberg remarked that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

    It has been revealed that svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Novo Nordisk ›.

    Shares of Novo Nordisk (NVO -2.70%) have fallen 70% from the all-time highs reached after it launched the first GLP-1 weight-loss shot. That has pushed the dividend yield up to 4.5%, well above the pharmaceutical industry average of 1.3%, despite a strong payout ratio of roughly 33%.

    Industry observers note that wall Street may not be giving Novo Nordisk enough credit, especially given the strength of its newly introduced GLP-1 pill. Here's why more aggressive investors may want to jump on this high-yield opportunity.

    There's no way to sugarcoat it: Novo Nordisk flubbed the launch of its Wegovy GLP-1 shot. The product was very well received, but the drug maker couldn't keep up with demand. That allowed generics to enter the market early, creating a major competitive headwind. When Eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) introduced a more effective GLP-1 shot, Novo Nordisk rapidly became the number two player. Investors' early enthusiasm quickly turned into deep pessimism.

    That pessimism persists, even after Novo Nordisk's successful launch of a Wegovy pill. Consumers prefer pills over shots, for obvious reasons. That helps explain why Novo Nordisk's pill launch has been even more successful than its GLP-1 shot launch. In fact, in the third quarter, the manufacturer estimates that the Wegovy pill captured eight out of 10 new patients starting oral GLP-1 weight-loss treatments.

    Sources indicate that the organization is executing so well that it increased its full-year 2026 sales and earnings guidance when it reported third-quarter results. From this perspective, Wall Street may be overly negative about the business.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But there's another problem that investors are grappling with. Novo Nordisk is moving to a volume-driven business model. That involves lowering prices, which has been a headwind for the top and bottom lines. In fact, while the tech giant updated its guidance, the sales and revenue midpoint is now flat. That's a massive improvement from the previous midpoint of down 3% for both metrics, but it is understandable that investors would remain concerned.

    Essentially, Novo Nordisk needs to prove not only that it remains an innovative drugmaker but also that its volume-driven model is working. And given the intensely competitive healthcare sector, it will likely see additional GLP-1 competition at some point. For example, Pfizer (PFE -0.51%) is hard at work on an acquired long-acting GLP-1 drug it purchased after the manufacturer dropped an internal GLP-1 candidate. That said, the global obesity market is very large, so there's likely to be plenty of room for more than one player. And there are also opportunities for companies to fill different niches within the still emerging GLP-1 market.

    For more aggressive dividend investors, the risk/reward balance is likely tilted toward reward with Novo Nordisk. The value opportunity here isn't just highlighted by the lofty yield. The stock's price-to-sales ratio of 3.3x is well below its five-year average of 8x. Its price-to-earnings ratio of roughly 10x is far lower than the five-year average of 23x. And Novo Nordisk's price-to-book ratio of 5.2x is a fraction of its 15x longer-term average. Notably, all of the ratios are lower than they were before the launch of the Wegovy shot. For reference, Eli Lilly's P/E ratio is nearly 45x.

    It has been revealed that given the success Novo Nordisk is seeing with its Wegovy pill and the improved revenue and earnings outlook, it seems like management is executing well as it shifts to a volume-driven model. Add in the lofty yield and attractive valuation, and the story gets even more attractive. If you can handle a little uncertainty, this well-run drug maker is probably worth a very close look right now.

    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:16PM EST.
    • Long-term investors view broad market sell-offs as offering discounts on growth stocks.
    • According to recent reports, dutch Bros operates a rapidly expanding network of drive-thru coffee shops, while Celsius markets functional energy drinks through global retail channels.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:16PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Dutch Bros ›.

    Long-term investors view broad market sell-offs as offering discounts on growth stocks. That's because, over the long run, stock prices tend to go up. So even amid some general uncertainty now, there could be good deals. Two such stocks we'll look at today are Dutch Bros (BROS -4.01%) and Celsius (CELH -7.36%).

    According to recent reports, dutch Bros operates a rapidly expanding network of drive-thru coffee shops, while Celsius markets functional energy drinks through global retail channels. Both companies are disruptors in the competitive beverage stocks landscape. This comparison looks at their growth trajectories and financial health to help you decide which stock fits your strategy.

    It has been revealed that dutch Bros operates a high-growth model focusing on drive-thru shops that serve a variety of hand-crafted beverages. The menu includes coffee, tea, lemonade, and the popular Dutch Bros Rebel energy drink. As of June 2026, the organization managed over 1,200 locations in nearly 30 states. Customer concentration is a factor to watch, as the company's brand recognition is somewhat limited.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $2 billion. This represented a revenue growth rate of roughly 30.7% compared to the prior year period. The company reported a net income of approximately $102 million during this same timeframe. This growth is driven by both new shop openings and steady traffic at existing locations.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Celsius creates and markets functional beverages that have gained significant popularity in the U.S. and international markets. Its portfolio includes brands like CELSIUS and Alani Nu, sold through convenience stores, fitness centers, and large retailers. The organization is substantially reliant on PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%) as its primary distributor in the U.S. and Canada. This single customer accounted for over 43% of revenue in 2025, and such high customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue for the organization reached roughly $3.2 billion. This reflects significant momentum with revenue growth of approximately 49.1% over the preceding year. During this timeframe, the company generated net income of nearly $230 million.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, dutch Bros faces intense competition from established coffee chains and other quick-service restaurants. Its high geographic concentration in the Western U.S. remains a concern, as most of its shops are located in that region. Rapid expansion also carries risks of identifying suitable real estate and maintaining its unique corporate culture. Regulatory changes regarding labor laws or potential drive-thru bans in specific municipalities could impact its operational model.

    According to recent reports, celsius is heavily dependent on its distribution agreement with Pepsi, which provides the backbone of its retail reach. This relationship creates potential conflicts of interest since Pepsi holds a significant ownership stake and board representation. The company also faces fierce competition from global players such as Monster Beverage (MNST -0.57%) and Red Bull. Additionally, integrating recent acquisitions like Alani Nu and Rockstar presents ongoing execution risks for the management team.

    Celsius appears more attractively valued than Dutch Bros, as it offers a lower earnings multiple despite maintaining a significantly faster revenue growth rate.

    According to recent reports, for investors taking the long view, broad market dips offer buying opportunities. After all, Dutch Bros opened at $35.50 on Nov. 16 and closed at $32.78 on Nov. 20. Celsius also saw its stock price dip, opening at $32.47 on Nov. 16 and closing at $28.46 by Nov. 20.

    Choosing between the two growth stocks for a portfolio, however, I would rather own Dutch Bros.

    One of the key reasons is that, as a growth stock, Celsius appears to be increasingly relying on acquisitions. In the third quarter of 2026, revenue for its CELSIUS brand fell by approximately 6%, and U.S. retail sales fell by 7%. It saw strong growth through its acquired Alani Nu brand, with revenue climbing 24% and retail sales growing 57.9%.

    Recent findings suggest that in comparison, in its third quarter, Dutch Bros grew revenue by nearly 30%, same-shop sales increased by 5.4%, and customer traffic grew by 1%. Granted, it's not an apples-to-apples comparison, given the differences in how the businesses operate. Still, it reveals that the growth opportunities for Dutch Bros come through its core offerings, as its stores are attracting more customers, selling more, and have future sales growth opportunities through new store openings.

    Recent findings suggest that while Celsius is buying growth, Dutch Bros is creating it. That makes Dutch Bros the stock I would want to buy for the long term, using sell-offs to pick up shares at a discount to where they could be trading in the future.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:18PM EST.
    • Industry observers note that should everyday investors favor a turnaround value play or a reliable beverage leader?
    • In a recent development, kraft Heinz focuses on household food staples and condiments, while Coca-Cola dominates the global non-alcoholic beverage market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:18PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Kraft Heinz ›.

    Industry observers note that should everyday investors favor a turnaround value play or a reliable beverage leader? This match-up explores whether Kraft Heinz (KHC +1.89%) or Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%) is the better buy for your portfolio heading into 2027.

    In a recent development, kraft Heinz focuses on household food staples and condiments, while Coca-Cola dominates the global non-alcoholic beverage market. Both companies provide essential products that often resist economic downturns, yet they follow very different growth paths and valuation models today. This comparison breaks down their latest financial results and potential risks to help you make an informed decision.

    Kraft Heinz produces and markets a massive global portfolio of branded foods and condiments, ranging from its namesake ketchup to Philadelphia cream cheese. As one of the prominent consumer staples stocks, it sells its products in more than 40 countries through retail and foodservice channels. Its largest customer is Walmart (WMT +1.51%), which accounts for approximately 21% of net sales, and this customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 26, 2026, revenue reached nearly $24.8 billion, representing a slight decline of approximately 1.5% compared to the prior period. The tech giant reported a net loss of roughly $3.5 billion during this timeframe, and its net margin was approximately -14%. These results reflect a period of adjustment as the company manages its global portfolio and navigates changing retail demand.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, coca-Cola is a global beverage powerhouse that owns or licenses hundreds of brands across categories like sparkling soft drinks, sports drinks, and juices. The company utilizes a vast network of independent bottling partners, including Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP +0.72%) and Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF +0.67%), to distribute its products in over 200 countries. It recently secured an exclusive pouring rights agreement with KFC U.S. starting in January 2027.

    In the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $51.1 billion, which represents a healthy growth of roughly 7.1% over the prior year. The company delivered net income of $14.6 billion, resulting in a strong net margin of about 28.7%. This profitability highlights the strength of its brands and its ability to maintain pricing power in various global markets.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Kraft Heinz faces intense competition from both major branded rivals, such as PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%) and Nestlé (NSRGF +1.24%), and low-cost private-label products. The organization must constantly adapt to rapidly changing consumer preferences and is dependent on key retail customers, who may reduce shelf space or pricing leverage. Additionally, supply chain volatility and potential future impairments of its intangible assets remain significant concerns for the business.

    In a recent development, coca-Cola is exposed to risks from unfavorable global economic and geopolitical conditions that can impact its international operations. The organization also faces health-related concerns regarding sweetened beverages, which often lead to increased regulatory scrutiny and shifts in consumer habits. Furthermore, Coca-Cola depends heavily on independent bottling partners and must navigate challenges like water scarcity and maintaining its brand image in a competitive landscape against PepsiCo and Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP +1.25%).

    Kraft Heinz currently looks cheaper based on its much lower forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and price-to-sales (P/S) ratio, suggesting it is priced as a value stock compared to Coca-Cola.

    Industry observers note that between the two, I favor Coca-Cola more for a simple reason: Kraft Heinz is executing a turnaround, while Coca-Cola is just executing.Looking at its recent performance for the third quarter of 2026, unit case volume grew 5%, organic revenue grew 7%, comparable earnings per share (EPS) grew 11%, and operating income grew 12%. Overall, that shows not only consumers buying more, but also Coca-Cola converting demand for its products into greater profits.

    Also promising in those quarterly results was that volume growth wasn't tied to just one geographic area, giving Coca-Cola multiple markets and helping reduce reliance on just one market.

    In addition, it's seeing success with its classic offerings, with Coca-Cola volume growing 5% in that quarter. But it's also seeing even larger volume growth with tweaks to its classic formulas, with Coca-Cola Zero Sugar volume growing 16%.     #73776. Industry News: Oklo vs. NuScale Power: Which Nuclear Stock Is a Better Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (775 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Oklo vs. NuScale Power: Which Nuclear Stock Is a Better Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (775 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:19PM EST.
    • As data centers hunt for power, Oklo (OKLO -4.75%) and NuScale Power (SMR -11.81%) have emerged as two of the most prominent contenders in the nuclear space.
    • It has been revealed that both companies aim to build smaller reactors that can sit closer to the point of use.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:19PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Oklo ›.

    As data centers hunt for power, Oklo (OKLO -4.75%) and NuScale Power (SMR -11.81%) have emerged as two of the most prominent contenders in the nuclear space.

    It has been revealed that both companies aim to build smaller reactors that can sit closer to the point of use. Oklo emphasizes fuel recycling and has unique partnerships, while NuScale focuses on a modular design already certified by federal regulators.

    In a recent development, oklo designs fast-fission power plants intended to serve specialized customers like data centers, industrial factories, and military installations. The organization is at the moment targeting major players like Meta Platforms (META -5.93%), Equinix (EQIX -4.89%), and Diamondback Energy (FANG -0.58%) for long-term power agreements. Because its business model revolves around a few massive potential contracts, customer concentration adds a significant layer of risk to the enterprise.

    Industry observers note that oklo does not yet report meaningful revenue, as it has not yet brought its first powerhouses online. As of Sept. 30, it had total cash, cash equivalents, and debt securities of $3.1 billion. For the first nine months of 2026, it recorded a net loss of $123.3 million.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Recent findings suggest that nuScale Power focuses on small modular reactors designed to be safer and easier to deploy than traditional large-scale nuclear plants. The company relies heavily on an exclusive strategic partnership with ENTRA1 for global sales and development. Key collaborations include work with the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVC +0.17%) and other project engagements.

    Like Oklo, NuScale does not report meaningful revenue. It ended the third quarter of 2026 with $1.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and investments. For the first nine months of 2026, its net loss sits at $135.2 million.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Oklo faces significant risks due to its lack of commercial operating history and the absence of binding power purchase agreements. The company is developing first-of-a-kind technology that requires complex regulatory approval from both the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Department of Energy. Furthermore, securing a scalable supply of specialized nuclear fuel remains a major hurdle for its future growth and operational success.

    Recent findings suggest that nuScale Power faces substantial risks related to ongoing securities class action litigation involving its disclosures about project prospects and competitive advantages. The business depends almost entirely on its partnership with ENTRA1, and any termination of that agreement could be devastating for its commercialization efforts. NuScale may still need to secure significant future capital to reach its commercial delivery targets.

    As neither firm generates meaningful revenue nor is profitable, it is difficult to rely solely on traditional metrics to make an investment decision.

    In a recent development, I could see the case for adding both Oklo and NuScale to a portfolio. That way, you can still make money from the upside of the nuclear energy market while not being tied to the success of either company. Still, between the two, I would rather own Oklo because of its unique setup. NuScale's success will primarily depend on selling its reactors, while Oklo has multiple revenue stream opportunities it can eventually tap into.

    In a recent development, it's a unique business model in that it attempts to develop reactors, sell energy and heat, recycle fuel, and engage in isotope production simultaneously. That does introduce more execution risk, trying to achieve multiple objectives at once, and it also makes it difficult to estimate the future value of what all that would look like when it's up and running. But the main takeaway is that, because of those opportunities, its sales-generating potential could be greater than that of other nuclear players.

    As mentioned earlier, Oklo already has some buy-in from big names, such as Meta Platforms. Oklo plans to develop a 1.2 GW power campus in Ohio that will support Meta's data centers in the region, and the agreement allows Meta to prepay for power and offer funding to advance the project.

    What Oklo could fully accomplish is still years away from fruition, so this should remain a small, speculative position in a portfolio.

    Shopify vs. Uber Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (781 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:20PM EST.
    • Choosing between Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) and Uber Technologies (UBER -3.25%) involves weighing two different tech stocks.
    • Sources indicate that shopify acts as the digital backbone for millions of online merchants, while Uber manages a massive logistics and transportation network.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:20PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Shopify ›.

    Choosing between Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) and Uber Technologies (UBER -3.25%) involves weighing two different tech stocks. Both companies have become essential to how we shop and move.

    Sources indicate that shopify acts as the digital backbone for millions of online merchants, while Uber manages a massive logistics and transportation network. This comparison evaluates their financials and business models to see which is a better pick for 2027 and beyond.

    Recent findings suggest that shopify provides the essential digital tools that allow companies to build their own online storefronts and manage physical retail locations. The tech giant serves millions of merchants in multiple countries, providing an all-in-one ecosystem for everything from inventory management to payment processing. By focusing on giving brands total control over their customer relationships, it has become a central player among tech stocks that support the broader e-commerce market.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $14.2 billion, representing an increase of approximately 32.5% compared to the prior twelve-month period. This robust growth was accompanied by net income of $2.1 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that uber Technologies operates a massive technology platform that connects people to transportation, food delivery, and logistics services. Its network spans over 70 countries, serving a growing number of monthly active consumers who use the app for ridesharing or ordering from local merchants. The firm leverages partnerships with major retailers like Best Buy (BBY -1.33%) and Tractor Supply (TSCO -0.77%) to expand its reach beyond traditional restaurant delivery into a broader marketplace.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $56.5 billion, which is a growth rate of approximately 13.9% over the previous twelve months. The firm generated net income of around $3.5 billion during this period.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    According to recent reports, shopify faces intense market competition from established platforms and niche providers that could limit its growth or force pricing changes. The tech giant depends heavily on third-party cloud infrastructure from Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) and payment processors like PayPal Holdings (PYPL -5.46%). Fresh risks involve the use of artificial intelligence, which could lead to inaccurate outputs or regulatory challenges.

    Industry observers note that uber Technologies deals with ongoing legal and regulatory challenges regarding how it classifies its drivers, which could fundamentally change its business model. It competes globally in mobility and delivery against well-capitalized rivals such as Lyft (LYFT -2.54%) and DoorDash (DASH -2.88%). The platform is also vulnerable to macroeconomic shifts, as inflation or rising fuel prices can impact consumer spending on rides and deliveries. Finally, the company relies on the mobile marketplaces of Apple (AAPL -1.90%) and Alphabet to reach its vast user base.

    Uber Technologies appears more reasonably priced as it trades at a much lower forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and price-to-sales (P/S) ratio than Shopify.

    Both are well-run companies. But if I had to pick only one stock, it would be Uber. It's not so much about anything Shopify is doing wrong; it's more about Uber growing its current business and the opportunities ahead.

    Despite Uber being a well-established brand, its recent 2026 third-quarter earnings results indicated that monthly active users increased by 14% to 215 million. Trips also increased by 16% to 4.1 billion, and gross bookings climbed 20% to roughly $60 billion. That shows not only that more people are signing up to use its platform, but that users are also booking more rides and deliveries.

    For its sales growth opportunities, the focus should be on robotaxis, which could be a huge market. According to research from Goldman Sachs (GS -6.71%), the global robotaxi market size is expected to reach $415 billion by 2035. By the end of 2026, Uber expects to have 700 fully driverless vehicles on its platform, with more than 2,000 in 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that shopify will continue to benefit from the growth of e-commerce sales. But for long-term investors, understanding that the roads over the next decade will be filled with more autonomous vehicles, Uber can be a centerpiece in that market, which should only grow in value.

    Management introduced crypto perpetual futures (perps), which are derivative contracts allowing traders to speculate on asset prices without an expiration date. Adding these products diversifies revenue away from traditional equity trading and expands options for active traders.

    Recent findings suggest that trading momentum continued through October across active retail accounts, and Webull is capturing market share in U.S. options. It relies on its global technology platform, multi-market compliance infrastructure, and product innovation to drive customer growth while maintaining expense discipline.

    With international expansion and latest asset classes scaling, leadership points to significant long-term runway across global markets.
